name: B10-0106/2026 – Motion for a resolution
title: MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the draft Commission implementing decision renewing the authorisation for placing on the market of products containing, consisting of or produced from genetically modified maize T25 (ACS-ZMØØ3-2) pursuant to Regulation (EC) No 1829/2003 of the European Parliament and of the Council
part_text:
The European Parliament is asking the European Commission to withdraw its plan to renew the licence for a genetically modified maize called T25. This maize is engineered to survive spraying with glufosinate, a weedkiller banned in the EU since 2018. Parliament says the safety checks missed long-term effects on soil, water, wildlife and health. It also says the Commission should not approve this maize when most member states did not back it. This is Parliament's opinion; it does not itself change the law.

- What changes: nothing yet; Parliament asks the Commission to drop the renewal plan.
- Who it affects: farmers, food and feed importers, and consumers in the EU.
- What happens next: the Commission decides whether to withdraw or keep its plan.
